record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Ordered and Orderable Groups
record.original_question: Let a tℓ-group contain two closed normal tℓ-subgroups and be ℓ-isomorphic to their direct sum. Is the group topologically isomorphic to their direct sum? 5

evidence.quote: 1.47. Let a tℓ-group contain two closed normal tℓ-subgroups and be ℓisomorphic to their direct sum. Is the group topologically isomorphic to their direct sum? 5

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological lattice-ordered group (tℓ-group) is a group G equipped with both a lattice order making it a lattice-ordered group (ℓ-group) and a Hausdorff group topology with respect to which the lattice operations ∨ and ∧ are continuous. A tℓ-subgroup is a subgroup that is simultaneously an ℓ-subgroup and a topological subgroup. An ℓ-isomorphism between ℓ-groups is a group isomorphism that preserves the lattice operations (not necessarily continuous), while a topological isomorphism between tℓ-groups is an ℓ-isomorphism that is also a homeomorphism.

Suppose G is a tℓ-group containing two closed normal tℓ-subgroups H₁ and H₂ such that G is ℓ-isomorphic to the direct sum H₁ ⊕ H₂ (as ℓ-groups). Must G be topologically isomorphic to the direct sum H₁ ⊕ H₂ (with the product topology), i.e., does there exist an ℓ-isomorphism G → H₁ ⊕ H₂ that is also a homeomorphism?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any publication resolving this question about tℓ-groups, closed normal tℓ-subgroups, and the equivalence of an algebraic ℓ-direct-sum decomposition with a topological direct-sum decomposition. No source confirming a solution (positive or negative) was located, so the current status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Direct sums and products in topological groups and vector spaces
status_evidence.snippet: There is an example of a topological abelian group G and two closed subgroups H and N such that G is algebraically the direct sum of H and N while G fails to decompose topologically.
status_evidence.claim: In the broader topological-group setting, algebraic direct sum decompositions need not be topological, suggesting the analogous tℓ-group question is delicate, but no result specific to tℓ-groups was found.
